newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam approves new foreign investment law.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam approves new foreign investment law.

text.p: Vietnam's official media said on Saturday that the National Assembly had approved a new law on foreign investment incorporating amendments aimed at improving the investment environment for non-Vietnamese firms.
"The law is designed to make it easier for foreign investors to do business in Vietnam," the daily Vietnam News said.
"The purpose of the new law is to encourage foreign investment and give priority to the transfer of technology, particularly modern technology, by simplifying investment procedures," it said.
"Those who slow the process of granting permission or violate the law will be punished."
Vietnam's foreign investment law came into effect in 1987, shortly after the communist government embarked on a drive to reform the command economy and open doors to the outside world.

The reforms, and the rapid economic growth which they spawned, brought a flood of investment into the country. Foreign businesses from 55 countries have now pledged around $22.6 billion towards projects in Vietnam.
However, only about 30 percent of that total has been disbursed, partly because of problems linked to red tape and an inadequate legal and regulatory framework.

Foreign investment approvals have been falling at a rate of 30-40 percent this year compared with 1995. The government, denying talk of investor disenchantment, says it has taken a more selective approach to projects, opting for quality rather than quantity.
Vietnam News said the new law allows hospitals, schools and science and technology research institutes to find foreign partners to attract capital and modern technology.

It also deals with the foundation of foreign-financed stock companies and the sale of shares in firms with foreign investment and gives overseas Vietnamese who invest in their home country a 20-percent tax reduction.
Full details of the law were not published in the official media.
Foreign lawyers in Hanoi said that, judging from drafts, the proposed amendments were not only limited in scope but also apparently aimed at protecting Vietnamese industry from foreign competition.
The drafts listed several areas where foreign investment would be encouraged, those where it was to be banned and those where 100-percent foreign-owned enterprises would be prohibited.

Telecommunications, insurance, auditing and electricity generation and distribution were included in the last of the three categories. Foreign investment in exploitation of forest products, wood processing and broadcasting would be banned outright.
